data.title: Palmoplantar keratoderma — viva
data.summary: Disorders of keratinisation · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Palmoplantar keratoderma** (Disorders of keratinisation)_

**Q1. Define palmoplantar keratoderma (PPK).**
- Persistent abnormal thickening (hyperkeratosis) of the palms and soles, inherited or acquired

**Q2. Discuss classification of palmoplantar keratodermas (PYQ).**
- Inherited — by pattern: diffuse (whole palm/sole — Unna–Thost/Vörner (epidermolytic, KRT9/KRT1), mal de Meleda (SLURP1 — transgrediens, glove-and-stocking, malodour, AR), Bothnian (aquaporin 5, aquagenic whitening), Greither's), focal/striate (pressure areas, linear — desmoglein 1, desmoplakin, keratin 1/16; pachyonychia congenita — KRT6/16/17; Howel–Evans), punctate (multiple small keratotic papules/pits — AAGAB; Buschke–Fischer–Brauer)
- With associated features (syndromic): Papillon–Lefèvre (CTSC — periodontitis with early tooth loss, psoriasiform plaques, pyogenic infections), Vohwinkel (GJB2 mutilating — pseudoainhum, honeycomb keratoderma, starfish knuckle keratoses, deafness; loricrin variant with ichthyosis), Naxos (plakoglobin — woolly hair, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy), Carvajal (desmoplakin — woolly hair, left ventricular cardiomyopathy), Clouston (hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia), Richner–Hanhart (tyrosinaemia type II — painful focal PPK, corneal ulcers, intellectual disability), Huriez (scleroatrophic — SCC risk), Olmsted (periorificial plaques, mutilating), Howel–Evans
- Acquired: keratoderma climactericum (menopausal women — heels), psoriasis, eczema, lichen planus, PRP, tinea pedis/manuum, reactive arthritis (keratoderma blennorrhagicum), arsenical keratoses, crusted scabies, secondary syphilis, myxoedema, drugs (capecitabine, venlafaxine, lithium, BRAF inhibitors), CTCL/Sézary, paraneoplastic (tripe palms, acrokeratosis paraneoplastica of Bazex — SCC of upper aerodigestive tract), lymphoedema, aquagenic keratoderma, chronic arsenicosis

**Q3. Write a short note on Howel–Evans syndrome (PYQ).**
- Autosomal dominant tylosis with oesophageal cancer (TOC) — RHBDF2 mutation; focal PPK (pressure areas of soles) beginning in late childhood, oral leukoplakia, follicular papules, and very high lifetime risk (~95% by 65 y) of oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — needs annual upper GI endoscopy

**Q4. What is 'transgrediens'?**
- Extension of keratoderma beyond the palms/soles to the dorsal surfaces (e.g. mal de Meleda, Greither's, Olmsted) — vs 'non-transgrediens' confined to palmoplantar skin (Unna–Thost)

**Q5. Investigations.**
- Family history, pattern, associated features (hair, teeth, nails, hearing, heart), KOH (tinea), biopsy (epidermolytic vs non-epidermolytic), genetic testing; ECG/echo in woolly-hair syndromes; endoscopy (Howel–Evans); screen for malignancy in acquired adult onset

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Mechanical paring, soaks, keratolytics (salicylic acid 5–20%, urea 10–40%, lactic acid), topical retinoids, calcipotriol
- Systemic retinoids (acitretin 10–25 mg/day) — effective but painful sensitivity if over-treated (epidermolytic types), lowest effective dose
- Treat hyperhidrosis and secondary fungal/bacterial infections, proper footwear and orthotics; surgical release of constricting bands (pseudoainhum)
- Treat cause in acquired PPK (psoriasis, hypothyroidism, drug withdrawal, tumour)

**Q7. Clinical patterns of hereditary PPK.**
- Diffuse (whole palm/sole — Unna–Thost/Vörner epidermolytic KRT9, Mal de Meleda — transgrediens, SLURP1), focal (pressure points — striate/ nummular; DSG1, DSP, KRT6/16 pachyonychia), punctate (many tiny keratotic papules — AAGAB punctate PPK type I)

**Q8. Name syndromic PPKs and their extracutaneous features.**
- Papillon–Lefèvre (periodontitis with loss of teeth — CTSC), Vohwinkel (mutilating — starfish keratoses, pseudoainhum, deafness — GJB2 or loricrin), Naxos and Carvajal (woolly hair + cardiomyopathy — plakoglobin/desmoplakin), Howel–Evans (tylosis + oesophageal cancer — RHBDF2), Richner–Hanhart (tyrosinaemia II — eyes, intellect), Clouston (hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia — GJB6), Olmsted (periorificial plaques — TRPV3), pachyonychia congenita (KRT6A/6B/16/17)

**Q9. Acquired PPK — causes.**
- Keratoderma climactericum (menopausal women), hypothyroidism, myxoedema, arsenic (punctate), paraneoplastic (tylosis, tripe palms, acrokeratosis paraneoplastica of Bazex — SCC of upper aerodigestive tract), psoriasis, eczema, LP, PRP, Reiter's (keratoderma blennorrhagicum), dermatophytosis, secondary syphilis, crusted scabies, HIV, drugs (lithium, venlafaxine, BRAF inhibitors), lymphoedema, chronic friction

## Quick spotter facts
- Focal PPK + family history of oesophageal cancer — Howel–Evans (tylosis)
- PPK + early loss of teeth — Papillon–Lefèvre
- PPK + woolly hair + cardiomyopathy — Naxos/Carvajal

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Palmoplantar keratodermas). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
